Cheap summons (Broodmother Spiderlings, Enigma Eidolons, Invoker Forge Spirits, Nature's Prophet Treants) or cheap illusions (Naga Siren, Phantom Lancer, Terrorblade, illusion runes) can be great for sending into Proximity Mined territory as sacrificial lambs to clear the minefields.

Stuns and other disables won't stop a Techies that's in flight from a Blast Off, but sources of forced movement or knockbacks can. This means cycloning or Force Staffing or Harpooning a Techies that's Blasting Off will cancel the explosion.
notes: Spells that move the enemy with vertical forced movement or knockback, like Sand King's Burrowstrike, Nyx's Impale, Lion's Earth Spike, and Rubick's Telekinesis, or horizontally, like Drow Ranger's Gust, Keeper of the Light's Blinding Light, Largo's Catchy Lick, and Storm Spirit's Electric Vortex, will also cancel the explosion.
Fears like Lich's Sinister Gaze or Lone Druid's Savage Roar can also cancel a flying Blast Off.

counters.text: Techies can do very little when getting hit by Clockwerk's Battery Assault since his cast animations take so long.
Avoid standing close to treelines when pushing against Techies. It's a favorite area for hidden Proximity Mines.
Techies players loooove going for offensive Force Staff plays, so be very wary if you see that item in his inventory.
Be very careful when walking up any high ground stairs since there may be a Proximity Mine or two hiding just outside your vision.
All of Techies' damage is magical, so items like Glimmer Cape or Pipe can improve your survivability.
Infused Raindrops can give you some very valuable early game survivability against a Techies.
Using Blade Mail against Proximity Mines will reflect the damage back onto Techies.

tips.text: The bonus damage charges you get on Refraction don't get consumed on denial attacks, but you also don't get the bonus damage when issuing deny attacks.
Since the entire damage instance is blocked, Refraction prevents Blink Dagger or consumable regen from breaking if you get hit.

You can survive a potentially lethal Oracle's False Promise by activating Refraction right before the spell times out. This is because the entirety of damage received (or heal received) during False Promise is delivered in one instance which can be absorbed by a single Refraction barrier.
Before going in for a gank or joining a team fight, you want a fully charged Refraction to be on the tail end of its timer so you can put a fresh one up when everything inevitably starts going wrong.

Meld has no cast time and no fade time. This is useful for disjointing spells, tower shots, and right clicks, but it's also huge for juking. When you're getting chased, Meld as soon as you get a moment of high ground above the enemies. If you're juking in the jungle, Meld as soon as you think you're in a split-second of fog. Chances are the enemy will assume you kept running and continue chasing the same direction.
You have no collision when you're Melded, so you won't block pathways.
If you have trouble landing Meld strikes in the heat of the moment, try using attack+move commands instead of right clicking on the enemy.
The armor reduction debuff from Meld works on Rosh. The debuff stacks as well, so you should try to double-Meld Rosh when you first start taking it.
Meld damage and the armor reduction debuff will be applied to all units the attack Psi Blade spills onto.
The "Meld Hit Bash" talent can stun enemies through debuff immunity/BKB.
The "Meld Hit Bash" talent will stun everyone who gets hit by the Meld spill.

To be an effective Lanaya, you've got to learn how to play Psi Blades like a concert pianist. A deny could be used to pick up a last hit in the same stroke. A full creep wave should be wiped in two spills after you pick up a Desolator. Move creeps and neutrals in the jungle around to get the perfect spills.

Psi Blade's spill angle is calculated from TA's position once the attack connects, not from where TA was when the attack was started. It's not much, but you can ever so slightly move yourself around after you launch an attack projectile to change spill angles onto the enemy.

You can target your Traps with deny attacks to give a target to Psi Blade spill off of. If an enemy is escaping out of your attack range or vision, try planting a Trap in a line behind them and immediately deny it to potentially spill onto the enemy.
notes: You can even spill Meld damage off of denying attacks.

tips.text: Psi Blade spill damage can hit ethereal units. If enemies have Ghost Scepters, you can try damaging the target by deny attacking your Traps to spill damage onto the enemy.
Psi Blade spill damage can hit invisible units.

Psi Blade damage can spill through Venomancer's Plague Wards, Techies' Proximity Mines, and Tinker's Deploy Turrets, but not any other types of ward units (other than your Traps). Probably because other ward units require a flat number of attacks to kill, but the Spillable ones have actual HP.
notes: However, Meld damage can spill through all ward units. Like if you're attacking a Phoenix Supernova egg, Psi Blade spills won't deal damage to targets behind the egg, but a Meld spill can.

tips.text: You can give shared control of your Traps to all of your teammates so they can detonate your Traps themselves by opening the scoreboard and clicking the "Show Shared Unit Control Options" icon in the bottom corner. Please notify your teammates that you're doing this otherwise you're going to sabotage their micro.

The core early game Trap locations for vision are the runes (or at least one rune) and choke points on stairs. Mid/late game should include Traps on the Twin Gates and jungle camps the enemy may like to farm.
notes: Traps don't give vision when placed inside the Rosh pit, but it's still worth putting a Trap in front of the pit entrance so you can catch when the enemy may be walking in to Rosh.

tips.text: Towers are extremely slow at killing Traps. If you're diving, you can plant a Trap in tower aggro range without fear of it immediately dying to tower shots.
Damage from multiple Traps won't stack.
The last Trap debuff an enemy is hit by will immediately overwrite the previous Trap debuff (for both the slow and damage).
If you are within ~1800 range of a neutral camp, you can draw aggro and stack it with Psionic Trap damage. Be sure to account for the Trap slow affecting the neutrals with your stack timings.
If you're close to messing up a stack, try using a Trap to slow down the neutrals before they make it back inside their spawn box.
You can use Trap damage on lane creeps to split push lanes.
TA is an excellent hero to learn Tread switching on since she can make use of all three attributes and frequently gets a Bottle.

counters.text: If you apply "overkill" damage onto a layer of TA's Refraction barrier, it won't start cutting into the next layer. Any single damage instance beyond removing a layer to 0 will be ignored.
notes: For example, if you Lion Finger of Death a TA's Refraction barrier, you'll only remove one layer of her barrier.

Damage over time spells are a convenient way to add damage instances that can help tick a Refraction barrier past 0 to start using the next layer. Batrider, Jakiro, Phoenix, Venomancer, and Viper are examples of heroes with spells that are handy at clearing off Refraction.
Items that apply damage over time like Blood Grenade, Urn/Vessel/Distiller, and Radiance can also slowly help tick Refraction barriers past 0.
Illusion heroes (like Naga Siren, Phantom Lancer, and Terrorblade) are good at dealing with Refraction since each illusion's attack could remove a Refraction layer.

counters.text: You can't break TA's Meld with any stun or silence since Meld invisibility is an infinite duration undispellable buff, not a channeled spell. Your team really needs to have ground targeted spells or detection (Dust or sentry wards), otherwise she'll just sit there until her Blink comes off cooldown.
notes: However, spells that change her horizontal position with forced movement or knockback like Batrider's Flamebreak, Clockwerk's Power Cogs, Dark Seer's Vacuum, Drow Ranger's Gust, Invoker's Deafening Blast, Keeper of the Light's Blinding Light, Magnus's Skewer, Mars's Spear, Primal Beast's Onslaught, Queen of Pain's Sonic Wave, Spirit Breaker's Charge, or Void Spirit's Aether Remnant can break Meld by moving her.

counters.text: Essence Distiller can provide true sight on the debuffed target, such as Templar Assassin in Meld.
Know what you're getting yourself into if you dive a TA. Can you handle her having Refraction? Do you have detection if she Melds? Will you be able to kill her if she has five Traps lying around?
Always be moving around when you're against her mid. Make her miss last hits because she's too busy trying to Psi Blade spill on you.
If you activate Glyph, Psi Blades can't spill any damage off of your creeps. Could be handy to know in a low HP mid lane skirmish situation.

If you're mid against Lanaya, get some sentry wards at around 5 minutes. Not only will this allow you to actually finish a gank on her if you get the upper hand and she tries to hide with Meld, but you can also clear the Trap(s) that you know she has on your side of the hill.
notes: If you have a spell that she can disjoint in the laning phase with Meld invisibility, it can be worth getting a sentry ward even earlier.

counters.text: Smokes are great against teams with a TA since they will often be lazy when spamming observer wards if they can rely on Trap vision. On the other hand, you need to be careful that you're not Smoking on top of a Trap.

Traps don't give vision if placed inside the Rosh pit, but she may have seen your team walking into the pit with a Trap in front of the pit entrance. All the more reason to Smoke into the pit when against a TA.
notes: Runes are also very commonly Trapped by TA, so she may see you if you're camping the rune before it spawns.

tips.text: Terrorblade's Dark Unity innate changes how much damage your illusions do depending on how far they are from your hero.
notes: Reflection illusions are also affected.

tips.text: Reflection works on heroes that are in fog, but not invisible heroes.

Reflection illusions carry all the auras that normal illusions carry. It's quite useful to cast Reflection on heroes with aura items (like Radiance, Shiva's Guard, or Assault Cuirass) or aura passives (like Beastmaster's Inner Beast, Drow Ranger's Precision Aura, Lycan's Feral Impulse, or Vengeful Spirit's Vengeance Aura).

Reflection illusions don't consider Terrorblade to be the damage source, so you don't need to worry about Reflection illusions damaging an enemy Blade Mail or Nyx Assassin's Spiked Carapace and reflecting onto your main hero.
Use Conjure Image illusions to stack the jungle, serve as wards, intercept an incoming creep wave, or deny runes in the early game.
Terrorblade illusions can only be in Metamorphosis form if the real hero is within 1200 range of them.

If you create an illusion on the exact same tick that Metamorphosis times out on your hero, the illusion will spawn in Metamorphosis form for its entire duration. This works with Conjure Image and Manta Style illusions, but is not easy to pull off consistently.

Each Conjure Image cast spawns the illusion in a counterclockwise fashion around your hero. Spawns will rotate between north of your hero, west of your hero, then south, then east, and repeat. Not particularly useful, but it is cool trivia.
Be aware that basic illusions (like from Conjure Image) have a fixed 800/400 day/night vision which is significantly less than a hero's base vision.
Sunder can be cast on allies and illusions (like Conjure Image or Manta Style illusions).
You can't Sunder debuff immune/BKB'd enemies or allies.
Sunder has a minimum HP transfer percentage. If you and a target are both below the percentage, Sunder will heal you both to the minimum.
If you use Sunder while in a "wraith" form, like from Wraith King's Agh's Scepter, you will Sunder the target as if you have 1 HP.

You can Sunder through Ancient Apparition's Ice Blast to gain HP. You can Sunder a Borrowed Time Abaddon to make him lose HP. Sunder is considered an HP swap; it doesn't behave as a traditional source of damage/heal.
Infused Raindrops can be super value on TB. He has tons of armor, but is very susceptible to magic damage nukes.
There is a brief delay when activating Agh's Scepter Terror Wave before the fear actually goes out.
Agh's Scepter Terror Wave will follow your hero as you move similar to a Shiva's Guard active.

counters.text: The Reflection slow and illusion can be removed with basic dispels.
Reflection illusions carry all things that normal illusions carry. This includes item auras, so be wary about building things like Radiance or Assault Cuirass against a TB.

TB has armor for days, but very little HP to back it up. Magic damage makes life for TB and his illusions hell. If your team is mostly physical damage, consider building Maelstrom or Shiva's (yeah I know I just told you not to build auras, but Shiva's is usually worth it) to clear his illusions.
Sunder. It's a spell. That swaps your HP for his. Something you should be acutely aware of when trying to kill him.
Any level of Dagon can instakill illusions. As do spells like Disruptor's Glimpse, Pudge's Meat Hook, Skywrath Mage's Mystic Flare, and any Hex.
notes: Brewmaster's Storm Brewling with Dispel Magic deals full damage to all types of illusions.

counters.text: Dazzle's Poison Touch when cast from his Nothl Projection applies a hex to all units hit. This is a useful tool for mass clearing illusions.
Enchantress can take control of enemy illusions with Enchant.

Illusions your team creates of an enemy Terrorblade will spawn in Metamorphosis form if the hero himself has it activated, but they won't transform if TB activates Meta afterwards. The transformation only works on illusions Terrorblade owns.
If you're a carry, consider buying a Revenant's Brooch to bypass Terrorblade's extremely high armor in the late game.
The Agh's Scepter Terror Wave fear can be dispelled by basic dispels.

tips.text: Your Leviathan's Catch innate will create fish if you've applied any debuff to an enemy hero when they die. Non-damaging aura debuffs, like Assault Cuirass, do not count.
The Leviathan's Catch fish never times out on the map, but enemy heroes can deny it.
Gush applies minus armor on enemies. Try to use it before Anchor Smash since Anchor Smash is physical damage.
The Kraken Shell active cannot be dispelled.

Anchor Smash is an extremely easy spell to animation cancel (hit the 'Cancel Current Action'/stop key during the cast animation). This is mainly relevant if you're laning against another melee hero since you can bait them out of getting last hits by throwing out fake Smashes.

Anchor Smash's damage is applied as an instant attack . This instant attack ignores disarms, has true strike, and applies attack modifiers (except cleave). If you have an attack modifier with a proc, it'll roll for a chance to proc on each target hit.
notes: Since Anchor Smash is an instant attack, it'll break your Smoke if it damages a unit.

tips.text: Anchor Smash works on ancient creeps, but not Roshan.
The "Anchor Smash affects buildings" talent also applies the damage reduction debuff to towers.
Agh's Shard Dead in the Water provides true sight and exposes targets who move into fog.
Agh's Shard Dead in the Water's fixed move speed even works on enemies who are hasted or have slow resistance.
The Agh's Scepter Gush projectile itself doesn't give any vision, but temporarily provides vision on every unit hit. The projectile can also hit invisible enemies, but won't give true sight.

counters.text: Tidehunter's Kraken Shell automatically strong dispels his hero after receiving damage over a threshold can be disabled by breaks.
notes: Breaks can be provided with items like Silver Edge or Khanda. Spells that Break include Doom's Agh's Scepter Doom, Hoodwink's Sharpshooter, Naga Siren's Agh's Scepter Ensnare, Nyx Assassin's Vendetta, Phantom Assassin's Agh's Scepter Fan of Knives, Shadow Demon's Agh's Scepter Demonic Purge, Viper's Viper Strike, and a few others.

counters.text: Kraken Shell can dispel a lot of debuffs, but certain persistent aura based debuffs like Disruptor's Static Storm or unit based debuffs like Grimstroke's Phantom's Embrace, can't be dispelled and are difficult for Tide to deal with.
Get a Magic Stick in lane if Tide is gonna be spamming Anchor Smash.
Ravage has a travel time as it expands outward, so if you're quick, you can attempt Force Staffing or using some other repositioning spell/item to evade it.
notes: You can even Blink inside of it as the tentacles move outwards since the Ravage AoE is a ring, not a filled circle.

counters.text: You can deny the fish he makes with his Leviathan's Catch innate if you attack+move/force attack (default a+left click) the jumping fish.

tips.text: Timbersaw's Exposure Therapy innate gives him mana for every tree he kills.
Whirling Death can be activated while you're mid-Timber Chain.
Be generous when targeting Timber Chain on trees. It's okay to sacrifice ~50 range to ensure you aren't whiffing Chains.

Timber Chain gives a very small slice of vision as it travels and gives a small radius of ground vision for a split second once it reaches max distance. You can use this to quickly scout inside the Rosh pit if you don't want to spend Chakram for vision.

If you Eul's yourself after casting Timber Chain, you'll fly up and the cyclone will get canceled once the Chain hits a tree. Use this to dodge enemies who may try to cancel your Chain cast with stuns.

Using Blink Dagger immediately after casting Timber Chain allows you to change your angle of approach to a targeted tree. You can use this to get Chain damage on an enemy and still quickly return to safety. You can also toss a Chain, blink into a creep wave and Whirling Death, and promptly fly out.

If you and your lane partner have amazing communication, you may be able to catch enemies off guard by having an ally plant an Iron Branch right on top of an enemy to give you a surprise Timber Chain target.

You can cast Chakram before Timber Chain connects or during the travel time to cut down on the Chakram cast animation. Timber will start the animation for Chakram as soon as he's in range of wherever you targeted it. Shift+queueing Chakram after casting Chain is the guaranteed fastest way to do this.

Remember that you can draw aggro from creeps on demand by right clicking enemy heroes. Even if the enemy hero is across the map, right clicking them will draw creep aggro to help build Reactive Armor stacks.
notes: You can even use the top bar portraits to draw aggro. If you see an enemy hero is in vision on your minimap, you can attack+move/force attack (default a+left click) the enemy top bar portrait and it'll issue an attack command which'll draw creep aggro without having to move your camera.

tips.text: Go into the jungle and tank a few neutrals to build up Reactive Armor stacks before a gank/dive.
The Agh's Scepter Reactive Armor active can be dispelled by enemies, but you'll deal the explosion damage when the buff is removed.

An enemy can receive the pass damage from the Chakram once when it flies out and once when it's coming back. So if it looks like an enemy is about to escape the AoE of the Chakram, just return it while they're still in it. The extra passthrough damage will be more useful than a few more milliseconds of slow.
The lower an enemy's HP, the greater the Chakram slow will be.
Timbersaw is disarmed when Chakram is out.

If you're trying to prevent someone from Blinking out when they're exiting a banish or Eul's or respawning from Aegis, don't expect a stationary Chakram to reliably cancel their Dagger. A Chakram in place only deals damage during set intervals. However, a moving Chakram checks for units to damage every tick that it's traveling. So time your Chakram cast/return so that it's moving underneath the enemy when they appear.
Learn the trees on the map. There are many unique juke paths that only Timber can take advantage of thanks to his skill set.
When escaping late game, try carving out paths with Chakram before Timber Chaining. Timber Chaining into a deforested area could buy you a few seconds of fog.
Agh's Shard Flamethrower can damage buildings.
Agh's Shard Flamethrower sets trees on fire as well. They will be destroyed after burning for 5 seconds.

counters.text: Don't stand next to trees when laning against or escaping from a Timbersaw. The distance you're saving by hugging the treeline won't matter when he purely damages your ass.
In lane, consider constantly cutting down trees if you have a Quelling Blade. You'll give Timbersaw fewer angles to Chain off of or fewer trees to get Whirling Death damage off of.
If you're a strength hero, Whirling Death's primary attribute loss debuff will make you extremely vulnerable in lane.

Timbersaw hates being silenced, especially if he has a Chakram out because that means he literally can't do anything. He can't attack because Chakram disarms him, and he can't return the Chakram because he's silenced.
Timbersaw cannot Timber Chain when rooted/leashed.
notes: Or more accurately, he can't cast Timber Chain. If he's already shot his Chain projectile, it'll still pull him even if he's rooted.

counters.text: If you stun Timbersaw at any point after the Chain projectile comes out, he'll stop moving. If your team has a shortage of stuns, save them for when you see his Chain come out as opposed to stunning him before he casts the spell. That way his Chain goes on cooldown, but he won't go anywhere.

If you have an Iron Branch in lane and wanna go for big plays, you can try planting a tree right in front of Timber when he's trying to escape and intercept his Timber Chain cast. Other players besides Arteezy probably do this, but no one cares when they do it.
Breaking Timbersaw will stop him from gaining new Reactive Armor stacks, but existing stacks will remain.
The HP regen Timbersaw gains from his Reactive Armor passive can be reduced by debuffs that affect health restoration:
notes: Items that can reduce health restoration: Spirit Vessel, Orb of Frost/Corrosion, Eye of Skadi, Crella's Crozier, as well as the "Crippling Crossbow" and "Jidi Pollen Bag" neutral item artifacts.

Spells that can reduce health restoration: Abaddon's Withering Mist innate, Ancient Apparition's Ice Blast, Doom's Doom, Drow Ranger's Agh's Scepter Hypothermia, Pudge's Agh's Scepter Rot, Slark's Saltwater Shiv, and a few others.

counters.text: Be mindful when right click harassing him in lane. Often times, Timber's prefer the Reactive stacks. Ideally you want to harass him with magic damage exclusively, if possible.
Chakram has a fairly slow travel time, so it's usually worth sacrificing some positioning if it means you can sidestep the saw when he's chasing you.
The lower your HP, the more Chakram slows your hero.
You can remove the Agh's Scepter Reactive Armor barrier with basic dispels, but Timbersaw will explode the moment it's dispelled.

tips.text: Mechanically, think of Avalanche as being similar to a mini Faceless Void Chronosphere. The Avalanche AoE is an aura that is constantly stunning. So throw it in advance if you know a hero will be in the AoE before it finishes (mid-banish, pre-TP).
notes: This also means that strong dispels, like from Abaddon's Aphotic Shield or Slark's Dark Pact, can't remove Avalanche's stun debuff.
Avalanche is also unaffected by status resistance.

tips.text: Toss fully disables the thrown unit (allies and enemies). It counts as a stun, so stagger it after Avalanche ends on an enemy to maximize disable time.
notes: Tossing enemy or allied heroes will break their channels.

tips.text: Debuff immune/BKB'd targets can never be thrown as a Tossed unit.
Toss damages enemy buildings if a unit lands near it.
notes: With Agh's Shard, Toss will even slow enemy tower attack speed if a unit lands near it.

tips.text: You can Toss people to runes.
Toss always grabs the unit closest to Tiny.
Targeting Toss on an enemy hero will pop their Linken's Sphere, but you can still grab a Linken's Sphere'd enemy and Toss them to something else.
notes: If you target Toss's landing on to an enemy that has Lotus Orb, they will Toss whatever you threw at them right back to you.

tips.text: While you do need vision of a Toss target, you don't need vision of the unit you're going to Toss. Say an enemy is juking in fog, you can just mash Toss on a nearby target and Tiny will immediately grab the nearest valid unit, even if they're in fog, and Toss them. Useful against something like a Tree Dancing Monkey King who you can't see.
notes: You can't Toss invisible units, though. So to clarify: You can Toss units that aren't visible, but you can't Toss units that are in visible. Got it? Good.

tips.text: When you're getting ganked by melee enemies, always be looking for units to Toss your aggressors away to.
notes: Next level plays when playing against any melee range Blink initiation: Bait yourself by hanging around in enemy vision and start mashing Toss on a target nearby. The moment you get Blinked on, you'll immediately Toss the enemy before they can react. Toss has an instant cast animation, so you should theoretically be able to beat any kind of Blink initiation. This could be useful against heroes like Batrider or Magnus who have to get within Toss range to initiate on you.

tips.text: If allies are caught on the edge of a Faceless Void Chronosphere, you can Toss them out.
You can Toss targets in or out of a Disruptor's Kinetic Field.
notes: With BKB, you can potentially go into a Static Storm+Kinetic Field and Toss allies out to save them.

tips.text: You can Toss an ally straight up in the air and it'll count as enough distance to cancel Ancient Apparition's Cold Feet even though it's z-axis distance.
Attacking a building with a Tree can splash/cleave damage onto creeps, but attacking creeps will not splash damage onto buildings.

When ground targeting a Tree Throw, the tree will disintegrate and damage the first enemy unit it collides into, ignoring structures. A Thrown Tree will not 'cleave,' but instead explode in a circular AoE around the target.
Throwing a Tree provides vision as it travels.

Tree Throw's damage is applied as an instant attack on the target hit. This instant attack ignores disarms, has true strike, and applies attack modifiers. If you have an attack modifier with a proc, it'll roll for a chance to proc on the primary target.
notes: Since Tree Throw is an instant attack, it'll break your Smoke if it damages a unit.
You can activate Shadow Blade/Silver Edge after the Tree is thrown to get the backstab damage on the target hit.
The splash damage from a Thrown Tree is not classed as an instant attack. So you can't apply Desolator on everyone hit by a Thrown Tree, for example, only the primary target.

tips.text: You can't directly target couriers with Tree Throw, but a skillshotted Tree or a Throw that explodes near a courier can kill the donkey.
Denial attacks with a Tree will consume charges but won't cleave onto enemies.

Let your right clicks finish. Tiny's attack speed is constantly changing throughout the course of the game, which makes it a real pain to consistently cancel his backswing animation. Err on the side of caution and be patient.

You can "store" the max attack speed second hit of an Echo Sabre/Harpoon by canceling the attack before it connects. The attack speed buff lasts indefinitely, so you can spend the first right click on a creep and then store the fast attack for another target.
Echo Sabre/Harpoon will apply the slow with every Agh's Scepter Tree Volley attack and not go on cooldown.
Agh's Scepter Tree Volley trees benefit from Agh's Shard Tree Throw buffs.

counters.text: As long as the rocks are flying around, an Avalanche will stun you if you walk into the AoE.
Avalanche completely ignores any sources of status resistance.
Avalanche's stun can't be removed with strong dispels (like Abaddon's Aphotic Shield) because it's an aura, similar to a Faceless Void's Chronosphere.
Beware of being Tossed backwards into Tiny's tower during the laning phase. If Tiny starts running towards you for no good reason, watch out.
Breaks don't disable any aspect of Tiny's Grow. Would be pretty funny if it did, though.
notes: Breaks do disable his Insurmountable innate, however.

counters.text: Tiny is all about burst comboing enemies down. Consider investing in HP items (Blood Grenade, Fluffy Hat, Bracer) if you're a squishy support that keeps getting one-shotted.

tips.text: Ice Shards has beastly range, but the projectile travels pretty slow. If you're going for a long range Shard, try to save it for when the enemy is moving into a chokepoint or just block the choke in advance.

The easiest way to 'reverse Shard' yourself is to target the cast of Ice Shards in front of your hero model, but inside of the white selection circle. With surprisingly little practice you can start cliffing yourself like a pro.
notes: If you want to take the guesswork out of it, you can also use shift+queueing. Right click to move as usual, then ever so slightly move your mouse ahead of that right click and shift+queue an Ice Shard right in front of your move command. If you want to go one more level, you can then shift+queue another move command after and you'll do the whole motion fluidly without ever stopping.
You can also use this technique to escape a Disruptor's Kinetic Field or Slark's Pounce leash.

tips.text: The Ice Shards projectile provides flying vision as it travels. The vision remains briefly around the Shards landing location.
You can use Ice Shards to help get vision of a neutral creep in the jungle to Snowball to if you're getting ganked and there are no good targets nearby.

Think about your Snowball target when trying to save yourself or allies. Don't always target enemy heroes, they may move in a way that'll drag you further into a fight. Instead, look for neutrals or lane creeps that will move you to a safer and more predictable location once your Snowball ends.
You, and anyone else you wrap up, are completely invulnerable and hidden/banished while inside Snowball.
Shrines of Wisdom do not count banished heroes for contesting/claiming the Shrine. So don't linger in a Snowball while on the Shrine and assume it's working.
You can pull allies into Snowball by right-clicking them. You can even use this while you're rolling mid-Snowball to pick up new heroes.
You can pull allies into Snowball even when they're cycloned. You need to have the "Right Click Allies" setting set "To Follow/Deny" for this to work, not "To Attack."
You can't Snowball allies that are affected by Batrider's Flaming Lasso, Enigma's Black Hole, Faceless Void's Chronosphere, or Primal Beast's Pulverize.
Allies can jump into your Snowball themselves if they right click it, but only if they're not disabled (stunned/rooted).
You can pick up runes while sitting or rolling in Snowball, but allies cannot.

Snowballing an enemy with Lotus Orb will put them into a Snowball targeting you once your Snowball lands on them. They can't launch their Snowball early so they'll be stuck in it for the full duration.
You can cast Ice Shards and activate Tag Team while you're in Snowball.
Tag Team damage works on neutrals and Roshan.

Tag Team's effects only work on attacks from Tusk, units Tusk owns, allied heroes, and allied illusions (though illusions only apply the slow since the damage bonus is "+green" damage which illusions can't use). Attacks from units/summons owned by allied heroes don't get any Tag Team bonuses.
Since the Tag Team bonus damage is calculated as "+green" bonus damage for each attack, you can cleave, lifesteal, and crit off it.
notes: The bonus damage also boosts Walrus Punch's crit, so always enable Tag Team before Walrus Punching for a big damage increase.

tips.text: You can cast Agh's Shard Drinking Buddies on all allied units, including creeps.
You cannot cast Agh's Shard Drinking Buddies while rooted/leashed, but you can cast it on allies who are rooted/leashed to move them.
notes: Drinking Buddies movement cannot escape Slark's Pounce leash or Disruptor's Kinetic Field.

tips.text: Agh's Shard Drinking Buddies movement destroys trees in your path.
You can Walrus Punch enemy couriers. Not really useful, but funny as a statement play.
notes: You can also Agh's Scepter Walrus Kick enemy couriers, but it won't damage them. This is marginally more useful since maybe you'll spot an enemy courier in Kick range but not Punch range.

tips.text: Walrus Punch attacks have true strike.
Walrus Punch breaks channels, even if the enemy is debuff immune/BKB'd.
notes: Agh's Scepter Walrus kick breaks channels, even if the enemy is debuff immune/BKB'd.

tips.text: Walrus Punch ignores Linken's Sphere and Lotus Orb.
notes: If you Agh's Scepter Walrus Kick a target who has a Lotus Orb buff, your hero will be kicked towards the middle of the Dota map irrespective of the angle you kicked your target.

counters.text: Ice Shards is dangerous in lane because of how it affects pathing. You need to add some extra space in your safe zone to compensate for it. The distance you have to move to walk out of the Shards doesn't seem like much, but you set yourself up for skillshot disables or free harass.
Tusk and all his allies are invulnerable and hidden/banished in his Snowball, so don't cast your spells until the ball breaks apart.
Tusk can't cast Snowball when rooted/leashed.

Lotus Orbing a Snowball will stick you in your own Snowball once Tusk lands on you. Since you don't have a Snowball hotkey, you can't launch it early, but you can pick up nearby allies and even cast your spells while inside your reflected Snowball.
Sources of knockback resistance, like Magnus with his Solid Core innate, reduce the distance you'll travel if you get Walrus Kicked.

tips.text: Are you dead? Are you sure? You should check. You may have respawned immediately thanks to your Ceaseless Dirge innate and have just been standing around in the fountain.
Undying's Ceaseless Dirge innate cooldown can be reduced with cooldown reduction, but does not interact with Refreshers.

Decay is a weird nuke. You take STR and deal the nuke damage on a hero with every cast, but it doesn't feel like much because their HP bar still looks close to full. After you play Undy for a couple of games, you realize that enemies will often fail to notice how much HP they're missing in lane and how much damage you've built up, so crank the aggression once you have a few Decay stacks.
Decay deals double the nuke damage to creeps.

In lane, try to use Decay only when you can catch multiple heroes. Even if the enemies you're laning against are trying to avoid one another, they'll eventually bumble into each other at some point. That's when you pounce.
notes: If you catch multiple clones, like from Meepos or Arc Warden + Tempest Double in a single Decay cast, you only get one stack of Decay. This is also true if you catch Lone Druid + Spirit Bear in one Decay.

tips.text: Enemies only get Magic Stick charges if the spell caster is in vision. Whenever possible, try to jam yourself into a little pocket of tree fog before casting Decay to avoid giving free Stick charges in lane.

In most cases, heroes try to lose as much STR as possible before using heals, like Wand, Salves, or Faerie Fire. STR from Decay does not work like this. When you lose STR from Decay stacks timing out, you will keep your HP number as opposed to keeping your HP percentage . Healing before or after Decay stacks wear off won't matter, they'll heal you for the same amount of your HP pool either way.

If you're getting ganked, use Soul Rip before spamming Decay. Decay increases your STR, but Soul Rip only heals a flat amount of HP. You'll heal a larger portion of your max HP if you use Soul Rip first and then steal strength.
Soul Rip searches for units around Undying to calculate the heal/damage, not units around the target. Units in fog don't add to the count.
Soul Rip is technically more useful as a heal than a nuke because healing isn't reduced by magic resistance.
You can Soul Rip your Tombstone to heal it.
Tombstone Zombies add to Soul Rip's unit count.

"Oh good, Flesh Golem is down, let's force a fight," said no team ever. Tombstone is your real ult, so use it carefully. The fight needs to get nice and committed before you should feel comfortable bringing the thriller, so avoid initiating with it.
Casting Tombstone in chases can be useful if you need vision since the Tombstone has 1200 day/night vision to match its zombie spawn radius.
Tombstone zombies won't spawn on targets that are in fog, but existing zombies will continue following any targets that escape into fog.
Tombstone is great for taking Rosh since Rosh will draw aggro on your zombies.
You can deny your Tombstone to avoid feeding the gold bounty. Remind allies that they can also deny the Tombstone.

Try to place your Tombstone in awkward spots enemies can't easily find in the middle of a fight. Like on cliffs or other nearby high ground areas. You can't hide it in trees very easily since the Tombstone will destroy trees in a small radius when placed.

Unlike many other banish saves, there are no restrictions to Agh's Shard Tombstone's bunker targeting. You can freely bunker allies affected by Faceless Void's Chronosphere, Enigma's Black Hole, Batrider's Flaming Lasso, or Legion Commander's Duel.
If a hero is inside the Agh's Shard Tombstone, they'll immediately be ejected and replaced by any other ally who attempts to enter the Tombstone, including Undying.
A Tombstone will spawn from the "Tombstone On Death" talent when dying normally or dying under Aegis.
Flesh Golem raises your HP when cast thanks to the STR bonus, so you may consider using it when escaping if the extra HP will help you survive a gank.
Each of your attacks in Flesh Golem will apply a slow and damage amplification Plague debuff on an enemy.
The Flesh Golem Plague damage amp debuff from your attacks fully works on Roshan.
notes: However, it doesn't work on the Tormentor because, unlike magic amp and armor reduction, barriers ignore generic damage amp.
While in Flesh Golem, attacks on Rosh will not spawn zombies. Attacks on Tormentor will spawn zombies.

tips.text: Debuffing an enemy with the Flesh Golem Plague damage amplification allows your team to damage targets through spells that usually provide 100% damage reduction like Winter Wyvern's Winter's Curse.
Flesh Golem illusions do not apply the Plague debuff or spawn zombies on attacks.

counters.text: Avoid standing next to your lane partner when you're against Undying. If he's spamming Decay, make sure he's only hitting one hero.

In most cases, heroes try to lose as much STR as possible before using heals, like Wand, Salves, or Faerie Fire. STR from Decay does not work like this. When Decay stacks wear off, you will keep your HP number as opposed to keeping your HP percentage .
notes: In other words, there's no benefit to healing specifically when you have a bunch of Decay debuffs. If you have 800 HP out of 1000 HP (80%), you'll still have 800 HP when 4 Decay stacks wear off, not the same 80% of your non-Decay'd HP pool.
Regardless, you should still get a Magic Stick if you're laning against this dude with how much he spams Decay.

counters.text: Dawnbreaker's Starbreaker, Ember Spirit's Sleight of Fist, Gyrocopter's Flak Cannon, Hoodwink's Acorn Shot, Kez's Echo Slash, Luna's Lunar Orbit and Moon Glaives, Mars's God's Rebuke, Medusa's Split Shot, Pangolier's Swashbuckle, and Void Spirit's Astral Step are spells capable of committing mass zombie extinction.
notes: Luna is especially strong against Undying since she can directly attack the Tombstone and all the Glaives will bounce around to nearby zombies.

counters.text: Axe can Counter Helix off zombie attacks, but it won't kill zombies.
Alchemist gets Greevil's Greed gold off zombie kills even though they have a 0 bounty.

Kill the Tombstone. Finish it. I don't want this toss-one-attack-I-didn't-do-much-damage-to-it-so-it's-not-my-problem or this well-we-almost-killed-it-but-then-it-got-Soul-Ripped-so-whatevs garbage. Unless your team has one of the aforementioned methods of zombie genocide it is almost ALWAYS worth killing the Tombstone the second it comes up. Even if you're faring okay as the carry, your support players are fending for dear life if you don't help them.
Snapfire's Lil' Shredder is great at quickly taking down the Tombstone.
Illusions deal ¼ the damage a hero does to the Tombstone.
Phantom Lancer can Juxtapose off the Tombstone.
Mjollnir is a fairly good pickup against Undying since zombies constantly hitting you will help Static Shield proc more frequently. The lightning(s) won't kill zombies, though.
Crimson Guard's active effectively neutralizes all zombie damage.
Zombies will lose interest in you and die if you go invisible.
You can see how much time is left on the Tombstone by clicking on it and watching its 'Spell Immunity' buff run down.

tips.text: Ursa can Earthshock to jump up or down cliffs and out of Disruptor's Kinetic Field.
You consume Overpower stacks on denial attacks.

The duration on the Overpower buff is longer than the spell's cooldown. Meaning that before you go in for a gank or into Rosh, you should cast Overpower well in advance so a second cast is already in the chamber when you need it.

When laning, try to keep Fury Swipe stacks up like you would Batrider's Sticky Napalm, especially against melee enemies. Ursa has very high base armor, so it can be worth tanking creep aggro to maintain Fury Swipe stacks.
Casting Enrage applies a basic dispel on your hero. Use it to wipe off damage over time debuffs, slows, blinds, or roots.
notes: If you get an Agh's Scepter, Enrage becomes a strong dispel allowing you to remove stuns as well.

tips.text: Fury Swipes works on Roshan allowing Ursa to kill him solo.
If Rosh is attacked by the team that killed him last, he'll release a "Roar of Retribution" at a certain HP threshold that enemies can hear globally signalling that Rosh is being taken.
notes: Roshan's Roar of Retribution disarm is not dispellable, so don't bother casting Enrage to try to remove it.

tips.text: Ursa is also very good at taking the Tormentor solo, just save your Enrage for the last few swipes.

There's a hidden item in the game called Block of Cheese. You make it by combining 18 Healing Lotuses and 1 Cheese. Most games won't have this happen, but with how much Ursa kills Rosh, it's possible.

counters.text: Ursa has no stuns, so keep your finger on your TP when you see him bearing down on you.
Ursa gets bonus status resistance while in Enrage. So if possible, try to save your disables for when Enrage ends, rather than during the buff.
notes: Eul's cyclone duration doesn't get reduced by status resistance which makes it a good counter against Enrage.

counters.text: You really need at least one Force Staff on your team against Ursa, preferably more. After that, Eul's, Scythe of Vyse, Aeon Disk, and Ghost Scepter are all good support items against Ursa.
Ursa can dispel himself with Enrage. Heroes with undispellable abilities like Invoker's Deafening Blast, Viper's Viper Strike, or Bloodseeker's Rupture are quite useful.
Ursa's Agh's Scepter allows him to Enrage out of stuns (similar to Abaddon's Borrowed Time), but he still won't be able to ult when hexed or silenced.
You can dispel Overpower stacks off of Ursa, making spells like Enchantress's Enchant's, Largo's Catchy Lick, Oracle's Fortune's End, or Shadow Demon's Demonic Purge fairly useful.
notes: Shadow Demon is especially useful since Enrage can't dispel Demonic Purge. So not only are you slowing Ursa to a crawl, but Overpower will get insta-dispelled if he casts it. Just try to cast Demonic Purge on Ursa before Enrage is active, otherwise Enrage's status resistance will reduce the duration of the debuff.
Applying Nullifier on Ursa is also useful for the same dispelling reasons.

counters.text: Breaking Ursa only stops him from adding new Fury Swipe stacks, it does not stop him from getting bonus damage from existing stacks.
Ursa likes to sneak his first Rosh very early on in the game. It can be worth the effort to plant wards around the pits early on if he's lazy and doesn't smoke into Rosh.

tips.text: Snakebite deals burst damage on the enemy every time they attack. Here are a few enemies that it really annoys:
notes: Heroes with spells that deal multiple "instant attacks" like Dawnbreaker's Starbreaker, Hoodwink's Acorn Shot, Kez's Echo Slash, Luna's Lunar Orbit active, or Pangolier's Swashbuckle.

Heroes that can't easily stop themselves from attacking like Legion Commander's Duel, Razor's Static Link, Windranger's Focus Fire, Weaver's Geminate Attack, or even Jakiro with his Double Trouble two attacks innate.
Heroes that have short bursts of high attack speed like Phantom Assassin's Phantom Strike or Ursa's Overpower.

tips.text: You can cast Snakebite on Rosh.
Are you struggling at maintaining creep equilibrium in the laning phase because of your Plague Wards? Watch this instructional video to help solve that problem.

tl;dw - Use the 'Cancel Current Action'/stop key and use unified unit orders. No one is forcing Plague Wards to constantly attack. Stop them if there are no heroes around, sic 'em all on a creep at the same time to last hit or deny, put them up on cliffs and tell them to shut up so they don't alert an enemy who didn't know you could see them.
notes: The "Unified Orders with CTRL" setting is also useful when chasing enemies down with Plague Wards. When you throw one up ahead, don't waste time box-selecting, just issue a unified ctrl+right click on the enemy hero.

tips.text: Plague Ward attacks apply a half-damage Poison Sting innate debuff, but the slow is the same value as your hero's Poison Sting innate.
Plague Wards have collision and can be used to block narrow paths.
Try to deny your Plague Wards in lane. Use your other Plague Wards to help deny dying Plague Wards.
Spam Plague Wards for vision. Seriously. Just slap them everywhere. They're super annoying for enemies to deal with and have 800 day/night vision.
When jungling, try to place your Plague Wards outside of the spawn box so you don't block new camps from spawning. Plague Wards last an eternity and will probably not time out before a camp respawns.
notes: Alternatively, Plague Wards are great for blocking enemy camps.

tips.text: The secondary Noxious Plague projectiles can spread to invisible and fogged enemies.
When spread Noxious Plague projectiles are launched, they will carry all debuffs that Veno has currently applied on the target and duplicate them on the secondary target(s).
notes: For example, if you have your Poison Sting innate and Venomous Gale currently ticking on the primary Noxious Plague target, the spread projectiles will copy the duration left on those debuffs and apply them to all targets hit by the secondary Noxious Plague.

This even applies to item debuffs. If you have Urn of Shadows or even a Scythe of Vyse with 1.25 seconds left applied to the Noxious Plague target, the spread projectiles will also apply an Urn of Shadows and 1.25 second Scythe of Vyse on all targets hit.

tips.text: Refreshers are pretty useless on Veno since all his debuffs are only refreshed when reapplied, they don't stack.

counters.text: Veno's Poison Sting innate damage over time is classed as "HP removal" so it does not cancel Blink Daggers or consumable healing. You can use a Salve/Clarity/Bottle without fear of it getting canceled.
You can deny allies debuffed by Venomous Gale.

All of Veno's spell debuffs can be removed with basic dispels (like from activating Manta Style or Lotus Orb). His Poison Sting innate, Venomous Gale, Snakebite, and Noxious Plague are all dispellable.
notes: Noxious Plague will immediately spread when dispelled.
Veno has a "Snakebite Undispellable" talent.

counters.text: You can't disjoint the initial or the secondary Noxious Plague projectiles.
If you're panicking in your fountain because you think you're about to die to Veno's damage, consider a few options:
notes: Buy a Faerie Fire.
Buy Blood Grenades.
Buy a Shawl if you have the gold. You can sell it back a few seconds later (but it turns your gold unreliable).
Pray.

tips.text: Manually casting Poison Attack on enemy heroes won't draw creep aggro.
Viper Strike works fully on debuff immune/BKB'd enemies, including the Break .
You can reduce the armor on buildings with the Agh's Shard Poison Attack.
Agh's Scepter Nosedive can highlight units in fog and invisible units if you pay attention to the particle effects.
You can use Agh's Scepter Nosedive to travel up and down cliffs.
The further away you target Agh's Scepter Nosedive, the longer Viper takes to travel to the destination.

Don't attempt to Agh's Scepter Nosedive through Disruptor's Kinetic Field or Mars's Arena. You'll get stuck on the edge and won't be able to act until their spell ends and your Nosedive finally finishes traveling.
Viper looks funny with high attack speed.
That's really all there is to know about Viper...

counters.text: You want to avoid putting damage over time sources on Viper. Every time he takes damage, Corrosive Skin will refresh on your hero if you're in the passive's range. Seeing as how Corrosive Skin is also giving him magic resistance, he'll typically take less damage than you from any damage over time debuff.
notes: This includes things like Radiance. You should probably avoid building a Radiance against Viper.

counters.text: Viper Strike's projectile can be disjointed.
Viper can't cast Agh's Scepter Nosedive if he is rooted/leashed.

tips.text: Shackleshot calculates latch angles based on where it was originally cast, not from Windranger's location on projectile impact.

For years man has wondered, "How does Shackleshot work?" Basically, it'll search for the closest available unit to the primary target to latch to. If there are no units in the AoE, it'll search for the closest available tree. It does not prioritize heroes over other unit types nor does it prioritize units in a straight line behind the main target.

What sets good Windrangers apart from bad Windrangers is how frequently Shackleshots are cast on creeps. Bad Windrangers will almost always target it on a hero even if there's a far larger window to miss the latch.

Shackleshot can latch to units in fog and invisible units. If you know where an invisible target is (like a Templar Assassin in Meld), then you can try to position a creep in such a way that you can shackle the invisible enemy hero as the secondary target.
Powershot gives flying vision as the projectile travels and the vision lingers for a few seconds at the end point.

Be aware that Powershot's massive range can also be a liability at times. If you're farming in dangerous areas, be careful with your Powershot angles, otherwise enemies may discover you're farming their jungle when they see a random green arrow fly by their heads.

If your hero is within ~1800 range of a neutral camp, you can draw aggro and stack it if you damage the camp, like with Powershot. Any further away and neutrals won't aggro your hero when damaged and just keep sitting in their camp.
The "Powershot Executes Enemy Heroes" talent adds Powershot nuke damage first and then calculates if the enemy is within the kill threshold.

Unlike Axe's Culling Blade, Powershots with the "Powershot Executes Enemy Heroes" talent can't kill enemies when they're under the effects of a buff that prevents them from going below 1 HP, like during Dazzle's Shallow Grave or Troll Warlord's Battle Trance.

Windrun gives you 100% evasion from incoming attacks, including attacks from towers. Even if a ranged attack projectile is already in the air, all sources of evasion calculate the dodge chance on projectile impact.

You can stop yourself from attacking a Focus Fired target by hitting the 'Cancel Current Action'/stop or 'hold' hotkeys. If you right click on the target again, Focus Fire will resume. Useful to know against Blade Mail carriers.

When moving in Focus Fire, you will face the direction you're clicking in, but once you stop clicking, Windranger will turn around to face the enemy she's attacking. This is relevant when Focus Firing a Medusa Stone Gazing so you can attack her and not get Stoned.
Focus Fire doesn't give vision on the target. If someone is about to escape in fog, use a quick Powershot to keep them in vision.
You can target buildings with Focus Fire.
notes: You cannot target ward type units (like Phoenix's Supernova, Pugna's Nether Ward, Undying's Tombstone) with Focus Fire.

tips.text: Focus Fire is undispellable and even persists on enemies after they die with Aegis/Reincarnation. You'll immediately resume attacking the target at Focus Fire speed once they respawn.
notes: If Windranger has Aegis, however, you will lose the Focus Fire buff when you reincarnate.

tips.text: If a melee hero reflects Focus Fire with Lotus Orb, they'll need to be within 350 + melee hero attack range (default 150) to land attacks on Windranger. Any further and the attacks will miss.

Despite its appearance, Agh's Shard Gale Force is not classified as traditional forced movement , but rather a "pull." This means it can't interrupt things like Magnus's Skewer, Phoenix's Icarus Dive, Primal Beast's Onslaught, Spirit Breaker's Charge, Techies' Blast Off, or Templar Assassin's Meld.

counters.text: Be acutely aware of Windranger's angle to you and any allied creeps between you and her in lane. Windrangers are always fishing for Shackles, so keep mirroring her movements to make it difficult.

Constantly keep her in your camera when laning against her. A full duration Powershot is not an easy spell for her to land, but it is if you're asleep at the wheel. Watch where she's aiming and move away.
Windrun gives 100% evasion against physical attacks, but physical damage can still hurt her. This includes damage from spells like Dazzle's Shadow Wave or Death Prophet's Exorcism.
Get an MKB or Bloodthorn to deal with Windrun evasion if you're a carry.
Windrun can be removed with basic dispels like from Enchantress's Enchant, Largo's Catchy Lick, Oracle's Fortune's End, or Shadow Demon's Demonic Purge.
notes: Nullifier, Disperser, and Eul's can also dispel enemies.

counters.text: Silver Edge's debuff applies a move speed cap on enemies. This can be a great counter to the move speed provided by Windrun.

Windranger will Focus Fire under any circumstances when she can normally right click her target. If she's stunned, slept, feared, ethereal, hexed, taunted, disarmed, or out of range, she won't attack.
Focus Fire involves a bunch of smaller damage attacks in a quick period of time. This makes damage block items like Vanguard or Crimson Guard very effective at mitigating her damage.
Blade Mail can make her think twice about wanting to Focus Fire you.
If a melee hero reflects Focus Fire with Lotus Orb, they'll need to be within 350 + melee hero attack range (default 150) to land attacks on Windranger. Any further and the attacks will miss.
The "Chipped Vest" neutral item artifact can discourage Windranger from using Focus Fire on you due to the return damage.
Venomancer's Snakebite deals burst damage on the enemy every time they attack which can be a huge issue for Windranger with Focus Fire.

tips.text: The Eldwurm's Edda item from your innate can be moved out of the neutral slot to a normal inventory slot.
To use your Eldwurm's Edda item innate, you have to right click on the item and select "Consume Item."
Arctic Burn's damage over time debuff deals a percentage of the target's current HP as magic damage. Your ideal targets are heroes who have the highest current HP, not max HP.
notes: As a result, the damage over time debuff can never kill an enemy. Some asymptotic damage up in this bitch.

tips.text: When in Arctic Burn, Winter Wyvern can't uphill miss on units or structures. Because she's flying. A rare instance of Dota following logic.
You can travel onto cliffs while in Arctic Burn to scout. Winter Wyvern has higher than average night vision (1200) making this even more useful.

The primary target of Splinter Blast does not take damage . I know you're really angry that Anti-Mage just Blinked away with 20 HP, but Splinter Blasting him does absolutely nothing. You're better off holding on to the cooldown in case the enemy walks into a creepwave or near some neutrals.
notes: Having said that, Splinter Blast is actually a dope Linken's Sphere popper because the range is ludicrous.

tips.text: You can target allied units with Splinter Blast, including your team's couriers. You can't self-cast Splinter Blast, however.
Splinter Blast's secondary projectiles can hit fogged units, but not invis units.
Cold Embrace the creep that's tanking tower shots when pushing; ideally when they're almost dead so they'll heal too.
Cold Embrace protects units from all physical damage. This includes damage from attacks or from spells like Death Prophet's Exorcism or Bristleback's Quill Spray.
Winter's Curse provides true sight on the primary target.
Winter's Curse applies a dispel on the primary target on cast.
notes: This is a rare example of a spell that can dispel enemies through debuff immunity/BKB.

tips.text: Debuff immune enemies can be Winter's Cursed if they're the primary target. However, debuff immune enemies will not be taunted into attacking an ally who's Cursed.
The more enemy targets caught by Winter's Curse, the longer the Curse duration. Enemy creeps and summons also add to the duration.
notes: Catching new enemy heroes can extend an ongoing Curse's duration.

tips.text: Winter's Curse taunts in the AoE for the full duration of the spell and follows the Cursed unit. You can Force Staff a Cursed enemy to catch fresh enemies or to drag taunted enemies deeper into your territory.

Winter's Curse can be cast on all enemy units, including creeps or summons. The situations in which this could be useful are far and few between, but you could use this to catch enemies who play it fast and loose with Blink Daggers (like Puck or Tinker) by Cursing a creep that's close to where the enemy will be. Or use it to bypass a Linken's Sphere if you just need a quick disable.
notes: Casting Winter's Curse on neutral creeps won't taunt enemies. You'll just force some neutrals to murder one of their kin for no reason.
Winter's Curse can be cast on Roshan and the Tormentor, but as with other neutrals, it won't taunt any enemies. It does make the target only damageable by Wyvern, though.

tips.text: Wyvern and any units she owns can damage Winter's Cursed enemies.
Allies cannot damage any enemies under Winter's Curse. Neither primary nor secondary Cursed targets.
notes: However, allies can still apply debuffs to Cursed enemies. Like stun/silence them, apply damage over time debuffs, build passive stacks (Ursa Fury Swipes, Monkey King Jingu Mastery, etc), or burn their mana.

Your team can damage an enemy under Winter's Curse (for a percentage of damage) if the target is affected by a spell that provides damage amplification. Examples include: Bounty Hunter's Track, Shadow Demon's Menace innate attack debuff, and Undying's Flesh Golem Plague attack debuff. The reason this works is because Winter's Curse is 100% damage reduction, but these spells make it so you're doing more than 100% damage on targets.

Instant kill spells, like an allied Ancient Apparition's Ice Blast, Axe's Culling Blade, or Windranger's Powershot with the "Powershot Executes Enemy Heroes" talent can kill a target under Winter's Curse if they're below the instant kill HP threshold.

tips.text: Most item/spell passives and attack modifiers are coded to not work on allies, so don't rely on an enemy critting or mana burning an ally under Curse to get a kill. There are a few exceptions: Slark's Essence Shift innate, Sniper's Headshot, and Basher/Abyssal bashes will work on allies.
notes: Muerta's Gunslinger technically works on allies but only if there are no other targets for her to Gunsling onto. When any other target is nearby, she'll start Slinging onto it instead of the Cursed target.

tips.text: Be sure to apply damage to any slippery targets in the Curse with a Splinter Blast before the Curse ends to make sure they don't Blink Dagger out. Remember, only Wyvern can deal damage to the Cursed targets, not your allies.

counters.text: Cold Embrace allows for a lot of easy setups for delayed/skillshot spells. Dumb Wyverns will often Embrace allies when they're in clear vision, so try to take advantage of the situation.
Revenant's Brooch can turn right clicks into magic damage allowing you to potentially penetrate Cold Embrace.
notes: The "Audacious" neutral item enchantment adds magic damage to your attacks.

counters.text: You can continue building 'stacks' on a Cold Embrace'd enemy with spells like Slark's Essence Shift, Bristleback's Quill Spray, Ursa's Fury Swipes, etc.
Don't walk into a Cursed ally. Think of the big snowflakey area like a Chronosphere because you will get sucked into fighting your teammate.
Ethereal Blade or Wind Waker can be used to protect a Cursed target from getting right clicked to death by allies.
notes: Pugna's Decrepify could also work.

tips.text: The Gris-Gris item from your innate can be moved out of the neutral slot to a normal inventory slot.
To use your Gris-Gris item innate, you have to right click on the item and select "Consume Item."
Paralyzing Cask can bounce to units in fog.
Linken's Sphere blocks Paralyzing Cask when targeted on a hero, but it'll continue bouncing afterwards.

The fewer units there are around, the more effective Cask is at stunning. In lane, try to pop an enemy with Cask after all their melee creeps die and only the lone ranged creep remains as a bounce target for maximum pinballing.
You can toggle Voodoo Restoration while channeling, such as during Death Ward or TPing.
notes: This is extremely important when playing against a Rubick to make sure he can't easily steal your Death Ward.

tips.text: If you're trying to heal allies with Voodoo Restoration, just right click on them to follow them (assuming you don't have right click allies set to attack), rather than starting the impromptu Dota Hoedown that always occurs whenever people are fumbling to get into the heal AoE.
Maledict can affect player-controlled creeps, like summons or Dominated creeps.
Maledict can be a good way to keep an enemy Blink Dagger on cooldown since it lasts for so long.
Maledict cannot be dispelled.

You can choose your Death Ward's target. If you have the "Unified Orders with CTRL" setting enabled, you can just ctrl+right click who you want it to attack and you won't break your channel. Or, if you have your hero and Death Ward selected and issue an attack command, it'll only send it to the Ward since you're channeling. Otherwise, just select it manually and right click your target.
Did you know that you can get one extra Death Ward attack off if you spawn it west of your target? It's true! Is this important? Almost never!
You can get Death Ward to stop attacking by issuing it a 'Cancel Current Action'/stop command. I think this would only be relevant against an Abaddon in Borrowed Time.
Death Ward can attack creep-hero units like Brewmaster's Primal Split Brewlings, Visage's Familiars, or Warlock's Golem.
Death Ward's cast range isn't too shabby. You want to try to exploit the full range every time you cast it so that enemies can't easily get to you to stop your channeling.
Death Ward requires vision of the target to hit them. Beware of casting Death Ward on low ground or near a bunch of trees because your target may escape into fog.
Death Ward provides vision around the unit itself (1200 day/800 night). The vision lingers for 5 seconds after Death Ward disappears.
Death Ward can benefit from the attack speed buff provided by Chen's Penitence.
Death Ward is frozen inside Faceless Void's Chronosphere. Place the Ward outside of the Chrono if you want to hit enemies inside.
Agh's Shard Voodoo Switcheroo's Death Ward behaves identically to a normal Death Ward. This means it benefits from Death Ward talents and the Agh's Scepter Death Ward bonuses.
notes: This also means you can control the target of the Agh's Shard Voodoo Switcheroo Death Ward by right clicking on the enemy you want to attack.

tips.text: You're stuck in the Agh's Shard Voodoo Switcheroo for the entire cast. You can't cancel it early, it's not a channel, it's more like a fixed duration banish.
Activating Glimmer Cape/Shadow Amulet/Shadow Blade will not cancel channels, so you can use these items in the middle of channeling Death Ward.
notes: Activating Ghost Scepter or BKB will cancel channels, so use these items before you start channeling Death Ward.

tips.text: Aeon Disk being triggered on Witch Doctor does not stop Death Ward from dealing damage since wards are considered separate units. Same reason why an enemy with Blade Mail won't reflect any Death Ward damage onto Witch Doctor.
notes: Death Ward being its own damage source also means that building spell damage amplification items on Witch Doctor will not increase Death Ward's damage.

tips.text: Death Ward attacks have 50% accuracy against evasion.
Agh's Scepter Death Ward attacks can bounce to creeps. This can be useful against zoo teams with a lot of summons/units.
Agh's Scepter Death Ward attacks will not bounce to targets in fog.

counters.text: Don't sit around next to your ranged creep once the rest of your creep wave dies. You're just asking for a Casking.
Maledict deals extra damage depending on the amount of HP you've lost since the debuff was applied. If you heal yourself, you'll take less damage on the next curse tick.
The burst damage tick from Maledict triggers once every few seconds. Try timing whatever invulnerability you may have (like from a banish) at those times.
Maledict's last few ticks can do a ton of damage. If you narrowly TP'd back to fountain, but still think you'll die, consider buying a Raindrop or Faerie Fire in base to help reduce the final tick.
Maledict cannot be dispelled.
Someone on your team needs to be dedicated to canceling WD's Death Ward. You only need one stun/silence/banish to completely shut it down.
Death Ward can't hit ethereal units. This makes Ghost Scepter a useful item if you're a support who keeps dying to the ult.
